steps.label: Shop.Api
steps.text: The shop has four projects. Shop.Api is the web app. It uses Shop.Application, which holds the use cases and the interfaces they need; Shop.Infrastructure implements those interfaces with EF Core and an HTTP client. Shop.Domain is the model.

steps.label: POST /api/orders
steps.text: Placing an order starts here. The endpoint sends a PlaceOrder message, and its handler does the work: it reserves each product, charges the customer, and saves the order. Every interface call continues in the class registered for it.

steps.label: IOrderRepository
steps.text: Repositories are interfaces in Shop.Application and classes in Shop.Infrastructure. On the left: who uses the interface. On the right: the class dependency injection gives for it.

steps.label: PaymentGatewayClient
steps.text: Payments go out over HTTP through a typed HttpClient, configured with PaymentOptions. If the gateway does not answer, the order stays pending.

steps.label: OutboxWorker
steps.text: A background service checks pending orders every 30 seconds. It is a singleton, so it creates its own scope to get a DbContext, which is scoped. Injecting the DbContext directly would be a problem Sightline reports.
